# Culturally Differentiated Launch: AI Emotional-Wellbeing Companion
## "One safety spine, one model, four cultural configurations"

---

## 1. Diagnose correctly: four dials, and "attitude to AI" is not the important one

The instinct is to treat this as a translation-plus-tone problem: same product, warmer copy in Latin America, more formal copy in Japan. That mis-specifies the problem. Four culturally-loaded variables move independently, and each one changes a *different* part of the product.

| Dial | What actually varies | Wrong response | Right response |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Disclosure norm** — who is it safe to tell? | Self / machine / family / professional / clergy / no one. Whether disclosure creates social debt or reputational risk | "Build rapport so people open up" | Design *what the companion is permitted to be*: confessor, coach, monitor, or record-keeper |
| **Idiom of distress** — how suffering is spoken | Somatic (fatigue, sleep, headaches), moral/spiritual (patience, gratitude, sin), relational (family, obligation), psychological (anxiety, boundaries, burnout) | Translate a Western affect vocabulary | Build the check-in around the *local entry point*; affect vocabulary appears later or never |
| **Unit of care** — whose wellbeing is it? | Individual autonomy vs. family unit vs. employer duty-of-care vs. state health system | One private personal account everywhere | A **trusted-circle primitive** with per-market defaults: off, opt-in, or prompted |
| **Locus of trust** — who vouches for you | Regulator, public health system, employer/occupational physician, government wellbeing programme, clinician-influencer, religious authority, peer word-of-mouth | "Add a privacy policy and testimonials" | Borrow the *locally credible institution's* legitimacy; the trust proxy is a distribution decision |

**Core insight:** the highest-leverage variable is **naming**, not intelligence. In high-stigma markets, the phrase "mental health" is the single largest conversion killer at the top of funnel — a user who would happily use a "sleep and tension check-in" will not download a "mental health app" that appears in a family-shared app store account. In Northern Europe, the inverse holds: euphemism reads as evasion, and a product that won't say what it does forfeits credibility with both users and regulators. **The same feature must be sold under four different nouns, with one set of claims underneath.**

**Second insight, the one that governs everything else:** unlike a streaming catalogue, this product carries **asymmetric liability**. The same behaviour — detecting risk in a conversation and doing something about it — is a duty of care in one jurisdiction, a regulated medical function in another, and an act that generates a legally dangerous record for the *user* in a third. The binding constraint is therefore not cultural taste but the **claims-and-escalation perimeter**. Build the safety spine to the strictest standard globally, route the response locally, and treat "what we are allowed to say we do" as a per-market configuration item with legal sign-off — not a marketing decision.

---

## 2. Global invariants vs. the Market Profile

**Invariants — identical in every market, no exceptions, no country-GM overrides:**

1. **Never impersonate a human.** AI status disclosed at first contact, re-disclosable on demand, and never denied.
2. **No diagnosis, no prescription, no claim to treat** unless separately regulatory-cleared in that specific market under a distinct SKU.
3. **A universal risk-detection layer.** Detection is global and identical; the *response* is locally routed. Human-in-the-loop review for all high-severity classifications.
4. **Emotional data is never monetised.** No advertising, no third-party sale, no targeting, no model training on identifiable content without separate affirmative opt-in. Enforced contractually *and* by data architecture, not by policy prose.
5. **Data minimisation by default:** derived state and structured summaries persist; verbatim transcripts have a short default TTL and require opt-in to extend.
6. **No engagement dark patterns.** No streaks, guilt notifications, variable-reward loops, or loss-aversion mechanics on emotional content. Session length is a *cost*, not a KPI.
7. **One clinical advisory board with veto** over persona design, safety copy, and escalation logic in every market.
8. **Age gating and a minors policy** that is the strictest of any operating market applied everywhere.
9. **Every market receives a configuration, never a fork** of the model, the safety layer, or the claims framework.

**Configurable (the Market Profile):** product name and category noun, persona (name, gender-selectability, formality register, avatar or none), modality mix, check-in cadence and prompt architecture, entry idiom (somatic/affective/relational/spiritual), trusted-circle default, faith-and-values content module, escalation partner network, data residency and retention, consent granularity, distribution channel, monetisation, and the approved claims set.

**Rule:** any market request that changes an invariant is not a localisation request — it is a request to launch a different product, and goes to the clinical board and General Counsel, not to the growth team.

---

## 3. The positioning engine: one product, four nouns

### 3.1 The vocabulary layer

| Concept | East Asia | Middle East | Latin America | Northern Europe |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The product | "Daily condition check" / self-care companion | "Space for calm and balance" | "Alguien con quien hablar" — someone to talk to | "Evidence-based self-management support" |
| The activity | Adjusting/ordering yourself; recovery from work | Reflection, rest, peace of mind | Desahogarse — unburdening; venting | Check-in, reflection, tracking |
| The problem | Fatigue, poor sleep, tension, work pressure | Stress, overload, worry | Stress, loneliness, money and family pressure | Stress, low mood, burnout, waiting for care |
| Words to avoid at acquisition | Depression, psychiatry, counselling, illness | Mental illness, psychiatric, therapy, "disorder" | (Few) — but avoid clinical coldness | Euphemism, "AI therapist", hype adjectives |
| Proof point that converts | Employer/occupational-health endorsement; discretion | Government wellbeing programme; total privacy | Affordability + availability at 3am | Published evidence, DPIA, data deletion |

The escalation of vocabulary is *intra-funnel*, not just cross-market: a Japanese user who has been checking in about sleep for six weeks can be offered clinical language; the same language at install would have cost the install.

### 3.2 The claims ladder — locked to regulatory tier

| Tier | Claim permitted | Regulatory consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 0 — Wellbeing | "Helps you notice patterns and wind down" | Consumer app in most markets |
| 1 — Structured support | "Delivers exercises based on CBT/ACT principles" | Borderline; requires evidence file, careful phrasing |
| 2 — Clinical | "Reduces symptoms of anxiety/depression" | Medical device (EU MDR Class IIa; ANVISA; regional health authority). Separate SKU, separate timeline |

Launch everything at **Tier 0–1**. Pursue Tier 2 only in Northern Europe, on a two-to-three-year track, as a credibility asset that then licenses stronger claims elsewhere.
